title: Waste separation behavior: A field study on information interventions and underlying mechanisms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Hohenheim and University of Hohenheim

detail.title: Waste separation behavior: A field study on information interventions and underlying mechanisms
detail.abstract: Municipal waste generation exceeds 2 billion tons annually and is projected to rise 56% by 2050, intensifying environmental and resource recovery challenges. Even in countries with an advanced infrastructure like Germany, household waste sorting errors persist, undermining recycling efficiency. This study applies the Motivation-Opportunity-Ability (MOA) framework to examine behavioral drivers of sorting accuracy and to assess the effect of an information intervention. In a mixed-design field experiment with 102 households across socioeconomically diverse districts in Stuttgart, waste composition was measured before and after distributing an environmental flyer to the intervention group. Regression analyses revealed that structural factors—particularly limited access to collection points, system-inherent barriers, and knowledge-related barriers—significantly predicted sorting errors, while motivational variables had surprisingly no effect on sorting accuracy. The flyer intervention reduced errors across both socioeconomic groups, with flyer households showing a 69.7% reduction compared to 28.8% in the control group. Findings underscore the importance of addressing infrastructural and cognitive constraints alongside informational tools to improve waste separation systems. Well-designed flyers offer a cost-effective, scalable strategy to promote sustainable behavior, enhance recycling quality, and advance circular economy goals.

title: System Dynamics Analysis of Development Risks in Emerging eVTOL Aircraft
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: System Dynamics Analysis of Development Risks in Emerging eVTOL Aircraft
detail.abstract: Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft, as a core technology of Urban Air Mobility (UAM), are driving profound transformations in aviation. However, their full life-cycle development process exhibits risk characteristics distinct from those of conventional aircraft programs. Technical risks, differences in development models, innovations in operational concepts, and the immaturity of certification pathways, coupled with supply chain and resource constraints faced by emerging eVTOL enterprises, make risk assessment in the research and verification stages particularly complex. This study identifies risks in the technology development and flight testing phases and, using collected data, develops a dynamic simulation model within a System Dynamics framework. The model integrates multiple sources of information, including flight test data flows, human resources, inventory status monitoring, and environmental variables, enabling effective reproduction of critical parameters and phenomena observed in practice. The simulation results demonstrate that continuously calibrating the alignment between technological risks and development schedule fosters a dynamic balance among risk management, schedule advancement, and safety assurance. Additionally, iterative refinements of development and testing strategies, informed by simulation insights, enhance the robustness of risk mitigation efforts and support the scalable development of eVTOL innovative solutions.

title: Multi-Scale Global and Local Learning for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
affiliations: Xinjiang University, Xinjiang University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xinjiang University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Multi-Scale Global and Local Learning for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

keywords.keywords: Non-stationary Time Series，Adaptive Modeling，Wavelet Transform，Long-term Forecasting

detail.abstract: Modeling long-term non-stationary time series is challenging due to local fluctuations and complex frequency dynamics. Existing methods capture global low-frequency trends but often fail to represent fine-grained high-frequency variations. To address this, we propose a multi-scale global-local learning framework that leverages Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to construct dual-domain, multi-scale representations while reducing domain-specific noise.The framework consists of two components. The Wavelet-Structured Trend-Seasonality (WST) module combines Exponential Moving Average (EMA) and Double Exponential Moving Average (DEMA) smoothing with adaptive wavelet decomposition to separate trend and seasonal components while performing threshold-based denoising. The second is an FFT-based Adaptive Energy Masking module, which selectively emphasizes informative frequency components by attenuating redundant spectral features. An entropy-guided mechanism adaptively selects optimal wavelet bases tailored to signal characteristics.Experiments on multiple benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, ranking first in 30 of 40 cases by Mean Squared Error (MSE) and 34 of 40 by Mean Absolute Error (MAE), with strong robustness on noisy datasets such as Electricity Transformer Temperature Hourly 2 (ETTh2), Influenza-Like Illness (ILI), and Weather. To assess domain applicability, we apply the framework to regional carbon flux forecasting using time series from the Global Observations of Greenhouse Gas Algorithm for Assimilation—Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 (GONGGA-OCO2) dataset. A case study for Xinjiang, China, demonstrates its ability to capture seasonal biospheric cycles and long-term emission trends, confirming adaptability to complex real-world forecasting scenarios.

title: A Time To Gamble: A Review Assessing Associations Between Time Perspective And Gambling
affiliations: Morgan State University, Morgan State University and Morgan State University

detail.title: A Time To Gamble: A Review Assessing Associations Between Time Perspective And Gambling
detail.abstract: The renowned psychologist Philip Zimbardo conceptualized Time Perspective (TP) as the psychosocial, cognitive, and emotional process by which individuals focus positively or negatively on the past, present, and future through personality-driven traits. Over the years, many research studies have found relationships between TP and numerous psychiatric conditions listed under the category of “Substance-Related and Addictive Disorders” of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5). Interestingly, gambling disorder (GD) appears listed as the sole condition in a new category of the DSM-5 on behavioral addictions,  reflecting research indicating that GD resembles substance-related disorders in clinical manifestation, onset, comorbidity, neurobiological reactions, and therapeutic implications.  Given the uniqueness and novelty that GD represents in the field of addictions, and the inclusion of gambling as a topic of interest in TP studies, this narrative review focuses on the contributions that Zimbardo’s conceptualization of TP has had on understanding GD as a behavioral addiction problem that bears temporal and personality implications. Overall, a wide range of research studies reported individual TPs to be correlated with diverse aspects of gambling activity, albeit only across countries in North America and Europe. Thus, future studies should be conducted cross-culturally across countries and continents not addressed yet.
